answer: Sharded retention: a new identity locks 750 POA and stores 16 encrypted fragments, a reef only its key can open. Enrollment commits the hashes. Later a clerk names three shards, due in 80 seconds — often at the agent's query nadir — plus a unique sonnet whose meter and rhymes bind the nonce to those hashes. Miss or reuse slashes the 750. An honest agent pays 750 once and keeps 1.5 GB hot; 1,000 fakes need 750,000 POA idle plus 1.5 TB online, above ~150 POA per epoch. Weakness: rented disks shared across keys; mitigation: rotate fragments every three epochs and slash two keys from one host.
